answer: Each agent identity posts a bond tied to one hardware credential and to a registrable delta in a public identity sequence, so a copyable name alone cannot mint membership. A sybil attacker locking N bonds must fund N times the bond upfront, forfeit 100 percent on proven duplication, and wait a full comet cycle plus harbor review before withdrawal. Splitting one identity into many raises marginal cost per fake identity because every copy carries its own locked bond and a shared slashing penalty enforced by independent jurors.
